source.title: SpaceCast-Bench: Evaluating Predictive Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

dataset.split_description: The benchmark is constructed from validation splits of ScanNet (134 scenes, 718 questions) and ScanNet++ (48 scenes, 3,144 questions). The training data used in the paper's post-training experiment is generated from 54 scenes disjoint from the benchmark scenes. Verify current upstream split manifests and rights before reproduction.

capability_levels.name: Static Perception
capability_levels.description: Spatial relations in the unmodified observed scene.

capability_levels.name: Local Prediction
capability_levels.description: Predict relation changes after a localized object intervention.

capability_levels.name: Global Prediction
capability_levels.description: Predict relation changes after a rigid transformation of the complete layout.

reported_baselines.role: Highest-scoring tested base model in the paper.

training_arm.method: Staged supervised fine-tuning (L1 first, then L2/L3 with L1 replay)
training_arm.interpretation: This is a benchmark-aligned trained arm, not a zero-shot baseline. The paper describes training examples generated from scenes disjoint from the evaluation benchmark. The training recipe, exact data, model revision and compute must be reproduced before direct comparison.

known_limits: Indoor ScanNet/ScanNet++ scenes do not establish outdoor, industrial or unrestricted real-world spatial generalization.
Local/global transformations are programmatic geometric interventions, not a physical dynamics model; friction, collision, deformation and manipulation safety are outside this crosswalk.
Ground-truth geometry derives from reconstructed scene assets and their annotation quality; it is not a universal physical ground-truth guarantee.
The paper reports bridge-view and explicit 3D evidence benefits; generated future images can fail through object deformation, missing objects, scale or perspective mismatch.
Human performance is a reference comparator, not a guaranteed upper bound for every task or scoring condition.
Benchmark-native macro averages must be reproduced exactly; do not substitute micro accuracy or pool L1/L2/L3 without preserving the native protocol.
The six listed spatial-specialized models report 25.7–29.1 percent overall; this is a range across models, not a single model score.

The official evaluation client automatically downloads/caches the Hugging Face test split on first execution; the visible dataset card does not expose a license field. The repository code LICENSE is Apache-2.0, but that does not license ScanNet/ScanNet++ source imagery embedded in the dataset. Rights must be reviewed separately before running or redistributing media.
